objective: Run bounded real-data ingestion pilots against Gaia DR3 and TESS/MAST, preserve reproducible input/output provenance and errors, and add regression coverage for a confirmed MAST API request-contract bug.
previous_knowledge_consumed: Issue #188 tracks multi-source validation and complete run provenance.
PR #189 adds the multi-source validation protocol, JSON run-manifest template, and append-only operation journal.
Existing source-backed acquisition and evidence-manifest infrastructure should be reused, not duplicated.
The CPVS membership mismatch remains an independent unresolved scientific blocker under #170.
The v0.2.0 scientific baseline and v1.0.1 release artifacts must remain unchanged.

baseline.status: Protocol, manifest template, and initial operation journal exist. Production adapters are not yet wired end-to-end. No Gaia/TESS run artifacts were previously recorded.

expected_improvement: Verify real access to official Gaia DR3 and TESS/MAST sources with bounded requests.
Record exact queries, timestamps, response hashes, schemas, counts, and limitations.
Repeat the Gaia request to test byte-level response reproducibility for a bounded sample.
Acquire one exact public TESS light-curve product and audit FITS structure, column widths/units, non-finite values, and quality flags.
Reproduce and root-cause a failed TESS product lookup, preserve the failed attempt, and add regression coverage.
Keep ingestion correctness separate from model validation and CPVS reference agreement.

gaia_dr3.repeat_test: PASS: second identical request returned the same bytes/hash and same ordered source IDs

tess_lightcurve.quality_flags: Multiple nonzero quality flags observed; documented recommended mask still pending

mast_product_lookup_incident.initial_failure: Mast.Caom.Products returned HTTP 200 and zero rows when obsid was incorrectly passed through generic params.filters.
mast_product_lookup_incident.root_cause: This service requires the observation identifier directly in params.obsid.
mast_product_lookup_incident.corrected_result: The corrected request returned two products, LC and TP.
mast_product_lookup_incident.regression_test: Added tests/test_validation_mast.py; current-head CI result pending.

scientific_validity.reason: Ingestion smoke tests are not model or cross-survey scientific validation.

measurement.trade_off: No scientific-gate relaxation; the CPVS discrepancy remains an independent blocker.

evidence: Two live Gaia DR3 requests were byte-identical for a fixed TOP 10 query.
A bounded TESS MAST metadata query returned five unique observation identifiers.
One public TESS SPOC light-curve FITS file was downloaded transiently and inspected; raw product not committed.
Initial MAST product lookup failure was retained; root cause was confirmed by a corrected request and successful product acquisition.
Added source code for service-specific MAST product request construction and fail-closed response validation.
Added unit tests for MAST request/response contracts; latest-head CI not yet verified.
No model evaluation, cross-survey feature mapping, full-vs-batch model comparison, or CPVS membership comparison was performed.

root_causes: The initial MAST product lookup passed obsid via the generic filters parameter; the service expects params.obsid directly. The corrected request returned products, confirming the cause.
other_incidents: A successful HTTP response is not sufficient: an empty result can indicate an incorrect service contract and must be treated as a validation failure when products are expected.

findings: For a fixed bounded Gaia DR3 query, the two observed responses were byte-identical; this is limited to those two calls.
TESS metadata ingestion and FITS product ingestion are separate stages and need separate evidence.
TESS light curves contain non-finite values and multiple QUALITY bitmask values; quality semantics must be documented before applying filters.
A generic HTTP 200 status must not be interpreted as successful product selection when zero rows violate the declared expectation.
The initial MAST API-contract failure should be kept in the incident ledger even after remediation.

open_blockers: Run latest-head CI and review all failures before merging PR #189.
Verify MAST request-contract regression tests pass.
Cross-check TESS QUALITY bitmask semantics and official product column definitions before deriving features.
Integrate the MAST/Gaia adapters with EvidenceManifest and the operation journal; live pilot records were created manually and are not yet produced end-to-end by repository code.
Add a FITS integrity/parser regression test using a small synthetic FITS fixture or approved test fixture.
Run a separate source-compatible scientific validation with explicit labels and object-level splits.
Keep CPVS membership mismatch unresolved until its own root cause is supported by evidence.

knowledge_carried_forward: PR #189 contains the current protocol, journal, and pilot evidence and remains a draft.
Gaia DR3 bounded ingestion and two-call repeatability passed for the recorded query only.
TESS metadata and one public light-curve product were acquired and audited; quality-mask interpretation remains pending.
The MAST product lookup root cause is confirmed; regression coverage was added but CI verification is pending.
Raw Gaia/TESS data are not committed; hashes and compact provenance records are retained.
No scientific model claims are supported by these smoke tests.
CPVS blocker #170 and baseline v0.2.0 remain unchanged.
